full_judgment:
6. Mr Md Jamiruddin Sircar, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioner submits that the Complaint Case was not filed in time in accordance with the mandatory provision of sections 138 and 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and, as such, it has become barred by at least three days under the said Special Law. According to his contention, cause of action arose on 22-4-2008 and after expiry of 30 days computing from 23-4-2008, the case ought to have been filed within 22-5-2008. But after expiry of 30 days of the date of receipt of notice, the case was filed on 25-5-2008. So the case is barred by limitation and it is useless to proceed with such case. Second ground advanced by him is that the instruction to the bank to stop payment of the cheque money by the drawer-petitioner-1 and bounce of cheque on this ground, does not fall within the mischief of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. Such instruction before presentation of cheque to the bank is lawful and no legal action is called for. In support of this contention, the case of Electronics Trade and Technology Development Corporation Ltd vs Indian Technologists and Engineers (Electronics) PVT Ltd and another, reported in Company Cases, Supreme Court of India reported in volume 86 page 30, has been relied upon. It is further submitted that the complainant did not disclose any fact about her alleged payment of money to the accused-petitioner either by cash, cheque or remittance and her claim on the dues for which the cheque was issued. In fact, the complainant and her son taking advantage of illness of petitioner No. 1, broke-open office of the accused-petitioner No. 1 and took away some blank signed cheques, which were kept in the office to meet emergency situation. By taking those blank signed cheques, the complainant had used the same for initiating false criminal cases. The learned Advocate further submits that the right of the parties accrued for distribution of share in the business and, as such, it is necessary to be settled by filing a case under the Company Act. Accordingly, the complainant has also filed Company matter No. 158 of 2008 for rectification of the share, which is still pending. So the case is very much civil in nature and the instant case cannot run simultaneously with civil litigation. So the impugned proceeding is liable to be quashed to prevent abuse of the process of the Court and harassment. 

 7. In reply, Mr Mohammad Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the complainant-opposite party No. 2, submits that the complaint case was scheduled to be filed on 23-5-2008, if the period of total 60 days is computed strictly from 25-3-2008, the date of receipt of legal notice. As the said last date of filing the impugned criminal case was a holiday (Friday) followed by Saturday another holiday, the complainant had to file the complaint case on the reopening day of Court i.e. on 25-5-2008. As such, there is no question of barring the case under limitation. Next he submits that the drawer's instruction to stop payment of the cheque comes within the meaning of dishonour of cheque for not arranging payment deceitfully, and such type of dishonour of cheque is also punishable under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. In suppat of this contention, the learned Advocate has cited the case of Faridul Alam vs State reported in 13 BLC (AD) 61. It is further submitted that all the disputes including issuance of cheque, receipt of notice, payment of money by the complainant for financing the Company etc are essentially factual disputes, if necessary, the facts would be decided at the time of trial on the basis of evidence to be adduced by the parties. But there is no scope to consider those disputed facts in this limited forum for the purpose of quashment of the criminal proceeding. The case of Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 44 = 2 BLC (AD) 16 is also relied upon to show the limited campus of the inherent jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, wherein principles have been formulated in the regard. With the aforesaid submissions, the learned Advocate for the opposite party. No. 2 has prayed for discharging the Rule. 

 9. To begin with the point of limitation, it appears from the Petition of Complaint that the cheque was issued on 8-9-2007 for payment of Taka 10 crores and it was dishonoured on 26-2-2008 on the ground that the drawer of the cheque gave instruction on the bank to stop payment. So, the cheque was bounced within six months from the date of issuance of the cheque. It further appears that legal notice was issued on 23-3-2008 under registered post with AD and it was received by the accused-petitioner on 25-3-2008 and the complainant filed the case on 25-5-2008 i.e. after 61 days from the date of receipt of notice (inclusive the date of receipt of notice). The learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner has strenuously argued that the date of receipt of notice has to be included in computing the period of 30 days for payment of money plus another 30 days including the last date for making payment. According to the submission of the learned Advocate, if the date of receipt and last date for payment are included, then it comes to 62 days on 24-5-2008, but Complaint was filed on 25-5-2008. Against such manner of computation, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 2 submits that computation of limitation period in every stage shall start running from the following date of the date on which specified time expired. It is contended that the date of receipt of the legal notice and expiry date for paying money of the dishonoured cheque shall be excluded for the purpose of computation as contemplated under section 138 and 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. Those dates cannot be inclusive. In this respect, the learned Advocate has cited the case of Mahalakshmi Enterprises vs Sri Vishnu Trading Co reported in Company Cases (Andhra Pradesh, High Court) Vol. 77, page 249, wherein it has been clearly decided that after expiry 15 days, the computation shall start running from sixteenth days onwards. 

 10. The learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner has also referred to the case of SM Anwar Hossain vs Md Shafiqul Alam (Chand) reported in 1999 BLD (AD) 166 = 4 BLC (AD) 106, wherein manner of computation of limitation period is available. It appears from the cited decision that the period of limitation shall start running after expiry of specified period for the purpose of ascertaining cause of action and last date of filing the case. 

 12. The words "within 30 days of the receipt of as Used in section 138(b) and 138(c) clearly give expression that computation of limitation period of 30 days shall from the following date, and last dates cannot be included for such computation. So, We rely on the view taken in Company Cases Vol. 77 page 248 of Indian jurisdiction and 1999 BLD (AD) 166, which are applicable in this case, for the purpose of computation of limitation period from the following day and not including the date of expiry at each of the stages. 

 13. In the instant case, we have already found that 30 days expired on 24-5-2008, which was the last date for filing the case. But we have seen from the calendar that in the year 2008, the dates 23-5-2008 and 24-5-2008 were weekly holidays, and, as such, the complainant had to file the Petition of Complaint on 25-5-2008, the re-opening day, which is permissible under section 10 of the General Clauses Act. In such view of the matter, we do not find any reason to hold that the case was filed beyond the prescribed period of limitation.
